Malevolent

muh-LEV-uh-lunt -- four syllables, stress on the second syllable, LEV. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Malevolent is having a wish to do evil to others.

The malevolent stepmother in the tale smiled sweetly in public while plotting the heroine's downfall.

Worked Example

The chess club's rival doesn't just want to win -- he hides the other team's clocks, spreads rumors about their coach, and grins whenever one of them stumbles.

A rival who actively wants bad things to happen to others is malevolent. Malevolent describes the wish or intent to do evil -- the ill will itself, whether or not any harm has actually been done yet.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

spiteful: deliberately wanting to hurt or annoy someone

malicious: intending to cause harm

vindictive: seeking revenge for a wrong

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

benevolent: wishing to do good to others

kindhearted: warm and caring toward others

Where it sits · how deep the wish to harm runs — spiteful → malevolent → vindictive

spiteful vs. malevolent: Spiteful is smaller and pettier than malevolent -- a spiteful remark wants to sting once, while a malevolent will wishes lasting evil on its target.

vindictive vs. malevolent: Vindictive is narrower than malevolent: a malevolent character wishes harm on others in general, while a vindictive one aims all that ill will at whoever has wronged them, determined to repay the injury.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — male-

root — male-: badly, ill (Latin male)

root — vol-

root — vol-: to wish, to will (Latin velle)

suffix — -ent

suffix — -ent: in a state of; doing (Latin -entem)

Put it together

Put it together: Malevolent combines Latin male ('badly, ill') with velle ('to wish') -- literally 'ill-wishing.' A malevolent person is one whose wishes point the wrong way: they want bad things to happen to other people.

Use the root in a new word: benevolent

Use the root in a new word: benevolent: The benevolent librarian quietly paid the late fees of students who couldn't afford them.

Root Check

Word Choice

Malevolent describes intent, not results: a malevolent glare, a malevolent scheme, malevolent forces in a story. Someone can be malevolent without ever succeeding at harm -- the wish alone earns the word. For harm actually done, reach for 'destructive' or 'harmful' instead.
